overview: A DockerLabs write-up focused on structured web enumeration, deobfuscation, credential discovery, and Linux privilege escalation in an authorized lab environment.
approach: I approached Internship as an evidence-driven assessment. I began with reconnaissance and service identification, then used the results to decide what to enumerate next instead of running unrelated tools. The workflow emphasized Web enumeration, JavaScript deobfuscation, Cryptography. Tools such as Nmap, Gobuster, Hydra supported the process, but the main focus was understanding why each test was relevant and documenting the path from discovery to validated access.
lesson: This lab reinforced how small clues found during web enumeration can become meaningful when they are correlated with authentication paths and local privilege boundaries. It also strengthened my habit of documenting why each hypothesis is tested rather than jumping directly to exploitation.
demonstrates: Clear documentation of an authorized penetration-testing workflow
